coptic_restorations.basis: Chapter-title preface, ~30 chars lost; final '-ⲙⲉ' alone gives no constraint on the heading formula or its referent.
Beginning of the chapter-heading line is lost (~12 chars). The shape '-ⲙⲉ ⲉⲧⲃⲉ ⲙ̄ⲙⲁⲛⲭⲗⲟⲟⲡⲉ' suggests a title formula, but neither the title verb nor its qualifier is fixed by the surviving letters.
End-of-title trail (~8 chars). 'ⲙⲉ' may begin a coordinated noun (e.g. another disorder paired with the ⲙⲁⲛⲭⲗⲟⲟⲡⲉ) but no constraint fixes it.

Five letters ending in '-ⲁⲗⲙⲉ' before 'ⲁⲛ ⲁⲡⲓⲕⲉⲟⲩⲉ ⲭⲉ' (= 'again to the others, saying'). Context demands a verb of speaking, but no Lyc. form '...ⲁⲗⲙⲉ' is securely attested for 'speak/say'; left unrestored.
Editor restoration: standard ⲁⲃⲁⲗ ('forth, out'). One missing letter ⲃ in the visible 'ⲁ[.]ⲁⲗ'.
Editor restoration ⲛⲉϩ ⲍⲛ̄ = '(for) him in'. Standard Lyc. preposition + locative across the line break.
Four letters between 'ⲁ' and 'ϣⲙⲉ' inside a relative clause about the fullness (ⲡⲙⲟⲩⲍ). No standard verb form fits the ⲁ-…-ϣⲙⲉ shape with confidence.

Two letters in ϣ[..]ⲧⲉ. Internal parallel: line 4 names ϣⲁⲙⲧⲉ ⲛ̄ⲫⲟⲥⲥⲁ ('three fossae') as the prepared containers; the immediate clause 'X within it' resolves cleanly as ϣⲁⲙⲧⲉ ⲛ̄ⲍⲏⲧⲥ̄ 'three within it,' summing the three vessels of containment.
Editor restoration of standard recurring frame ⲍⲁⲧⲉⲍⲏ ⲁⲛ ⲉⲙⲡⲁⲧⲉ 'beforehand again, before…' which structures the whole kephalaion.

Greek loan ending '-ⲥⲓⲁ', ~4 chars. ⲉⲝⲟⲩⲥⲓⲁ ('authority/power') fits the count and matches the cosmological logic: the archonic 'authority' is the agent that 'manifests forth the worlds' in the next clause, paralleling the self-side actors elsewhere in the teaching. Editor's alternative ⲡⲁⲣⲟⲩⲥⲓⲁ would require 5 chars.
Nine letters between 'ⲛ̄ⲛ̄ⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ' ('the worlds') and 'ⲡⲕⲁⲍ' ('the earth'). Likely a coordinating phrase (e.g. ⲙⲛ̄ ⲡⲏⲩⲉ ⲙⲛ̄), but no formula of the corpus fixes it; left unrestored.
Two letters at end of clause after 'ⲡⲕⲁⲍ'. Likely a connective ⲙⲛ̄ ('and') or pronoun, but unconstrained.

Three letters terminating in ⲍ before visible 'ⲉⲓⲉ' (ⲍⲉⲓⲉ = ϩⲉⲓⲉ 'fall'). The third-person singular preformative ⲁϥ- + initial ⲍ of ⲍⲉⲓⲉ yields ⲁϥⲍⲉⲓⲉ 'he fell,' the only form fitting both the trace and the 'before X fell to the sea of Enthumesis' clause.

Editor restores article ⲡ; 3-4 chars total. The Father of Life 'establishes a place for him in the earth' (ⲡⲕⲁⲍ) — i.e. the natural mind as ground-substrate, fitting the teaching's logic that even what falls falls into a prepared place. Other 4-char options (e.g. ⲡⲏⲩⲉ 'heavens') do not fit a fall-receptacle.
Two letters in 'ⲙⲁⲙ[..]ⲉⲓⲥ'. Possibilities (ⲡⲱ giving ⲙⲁⲙⲡⲱⲉⲓⲥ 'place of the master') exist but none is fixed by the trace or by parallel; left unrestored.
Editor restoration: ⲛⲧⲟⲩⲉⲩⲉ (Lyc. plural of ⲧⲟⲟⲩ 'mountain') — 'the mountains of the heavens that are above.' Trace '-ⲉⲩⲉ' is the plural ending.
Five letters at end of line after 'ⲙⲙⲁⲣⲱ' (harbors). Genitive complement expected ('harbors of …') but unconstrained.
Marked 'abgerieben' (rubbed off) by the editor; eight characters of ink physically lost. No restoration possible.
Editor restoration: completes 'the Palamas of the Light beckoned (ⲭⲱⲣⲙⲉ = ϫⲱⲣⲙ̄) after her — to (that place).' Fits the immediately following 'ⲡⲙⲁ ⲉⲧⲙⲙⲉⲩ' continuation.
Seven letters between 'ⲁⲛ' and 'ⲁϩⲧⲱⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧϩ' ('he stood fast upon him'). Subject is anaphoric (Adamas/Palamas already named), and the slot may hold a connective + pronoun, but no formula fixes it.
Editor restoration of γέενναι 'Gehennas' (ⲍⲉⲛⲧⲉⲉⲛⲛⲁ) — the prepared dark prison-realms that grasp Error and the dregs of darkness, paralleling the abyss-prison of the Watchers below.
Editor restoration completing the verbal form ⲉⲩⲁⲣⲁⲧⲉ ⲛ̄- 'that they may grasp/seize-' (ⲱⲣϫ ⲛ-).
Editor restoration: standard locution ⲧⲟⲓⲛ-ⲃⲱⲗ-ⲁⲃⲁⲗ ('the dissolution-forth') = 'until the dissolution of the world,' matching corpus eschatological vocabulary.
Editor restoration of qualitative ⲃⲱⲟⲥ 'are clothed,' confirmed by the verb's full repetition at the start of the next line ('ⲃⲱⲟⲥ ⲍⲛ̄ ⲧⲁⲣⲭⲟⲛⲧⲓⲕⲏ').

Editor restoration: Greek τάγμα 'rank/order' as the cosmic 'orders' of the dark powers. 'Whose orders are clothed in the archonic host' fits the kephalaion's vocabulary of organized self-loving formations.
Editor restoration repeating ⲧⲁⲣⲭⲟⲛⲧⲓⲕⲏ 'archonic host' from the immediately preceding clause, parallel structure 'in the archonic host, in the archonic [host] which is upper-side and lower-side.'
Long lacuna (~18 chars) at line end. No formula or trace constrains it; the surviving 'ⲛⲉⲧ-' at gap-edge could begin many relative constructions.
Editor restoration: relative + locative ⲉⲧ-ⲥⲍⲛ̄ 'who are in (their heart).' Single letter ⲉ before visible 'ⲧⲥⲍⲛ̄'.
Editor restoration: beginning of ⲁⲧⲩⲣⲁⲛⲛⲉⲩⲉ ('they tyrannize') split across the line break, completing the visible 'ⲣⲁⲛⲛⲉⲩⲉ' on the next line.
Editor restoration: Lyc. ⲕⲁⲟⲟⲗⲉ (= ⲕⲗⲟⲟⲗⲉ 'cloud') in plural with article ⲛ-. Fits the paratactic catalogue 'dark beasts and clouds and winds and spirits and birds.'
Editor restoration completing ⲧⲏⲩ 'winds' + connective ⲙⲛ̄ 'and,' continuing the catalogue.
Editor restoration: ⲛⲑⲁⲗⲁⲥⲥⲁ 'sea,' completing ⲧⲛⲁⲟ ⲛ̄ⲑⲁⲗⲁⲥⲥⲁ 'great sea' across the line break — the salt-sea outside the seven firmaments where the self-host is contained.

Editor restores ⲡⲕⲉⲕⲉ 'the Darkness'; remaining ~8 chars filled with ⲙ̄ⲡⲛⲟⲩⲛ ('of the abyss'), giving 'into the abyss with the darkness of the abyss' — the canonical pairing in the corpus where the self is bound at its lowest state.

Long lacuna (~16 chars) following 'before the abortions.' Context demands a verb of falling/coming-to-the-earth, but the specific construction (whether ⲣⲱⲣⲡ ⲁⲡⲓⲧⲛⲉ, ⲁⲩⲉⲓ ⲁⲡⲓⲧⲛⲉ, or another form) is not constrained.

One letter before the visible ⲍ. The directional ⲁⲍⲟⲩⲛ ('inward') matches both the trace and the parallel in the next line ('ⲥⲁⲩⲍⲟⲩ ⲁⲍⲟⲩⲛ' — they gathered them inward), and fits the teaching's claim that abortions are gathered inward into a prepared dwelling.
16 chars at line end. Likely a parallel ⲁⲩⲥⲙⲓⲛⲉ-clause establishing a dwelling for the abortions, but unconstrained in detail.
Editor restoration: standard recurring frame-adverb ϩⲁ-ⲧⲉ-ϩⲏ 'beforehand,' opening another instance of the kephalaion's scaffolding clause.
Editor restoration: 'before they begot,' completing the ⲍⲁⲧⲉⲍⲏ ⲉⲙⲡⲁⲧⲟⲩ- frame with the verb ⲭⲡⲟ 'beget.'
Editor restoration: negative particle ⲉⲛ required by the qualitative-relative 'who knew not (a righteousness)' — antithesis with the godliness mentioned in the next line.
Editor restoration: Greek δικαιοσύνη 'righteousness'; visible '-ⲟⲩ-' and final '-ⲟⲥⲩⲛⲏ' fix the lemma. Fits the antithesis 'knew not righteousness, with godliness — they ordered…'.
Editor restoration: ⲥⲙⲓⲛⲉ 'establish, set up' after visible ⲁⲩⲥ-. Direct parallel to ⲁⲩⲥⲙⲓⲛⲉ in line 4 ('they established three fossae'); here they establish twelve cities.
Editor restoration: completes 'sons of the Giants' + future auxiliary ⲛⲁ-. The pattern ⲉⲣⲉ ⲛⲱⲏⲣⲉ ⲛ̄ⲛⲅⲓⲅⲁⲥ ⲛⲁ-ⲟⲩⲱⲍ requires this fill.
Editor restoration: completes ⲉⲣⲏⲩ 'each other' + relative head ⲛⲉ- before ⲧⲉⲱⲁⲩⲇ ('would'). Standard distributive idiom.

Verb governing 'the fullness' (ⲡⲙⲟⲩⲍ) is lost; English left as a placeholder.

Coptic [ⲉⲝⲟⲩ]ⲥⲓⲁ 'authority/power' as the agent that 'manifested forth the worlds' in the next clause — the archonic 'authority,' fitting the teaching's logic that the self-side actors are answered by the Father of Life's prepared structures.

restoration_note: The teaching is structured around a recurring 'ⲍⲁⲧⲉⲍⲏ ⲉⲙⲡⲁⲧⲟⲩ-' frame ('beforehand, before they …') in which each disorder of the self — places of deceit, the boundary of the sea, the disordered natural falling into Enthumesis, Error and the dregs of darkness, the bexeue/archonic host, the abortions, the Watchers and Giants — is met by a containment-structure prepared in advance by the Father of Life. The repetition fixed many gaps directly: editor-restored spans for the recurring frame (gap 8, 36, 37), standard particles (4, 5, 27, 28, 38), formula-internal repetitions (23, 25, 30, 31), and Greek-loan technical terms whose stems are partially visible (20 Gehennas, 22 ⲃⲱⲗ-ⲁⲃⲁⲗ, 24 τάγμα, 39 δικαιοσύνη). Internal parallels resolve gap 7 (ϣⲁⲙⲧⲉ 'three' from the three fossae of line 4) and gap 40 (ⲥⲙⲓⲛⲉ matching the verb of line 4). Gap 12 (ⲁϥⲍ) and gap 34 (ⲁ → ⲁⲍⲟⲩⲛ) are constrained by the surviving traces and immediate semantics. Gap 9 ([ⲉⲝⲟⲩ]ⲥⲓⲁ) and gap 32 (ⲡⲕⲉⲕⲉ ⲙ̄ⲡⲛⲟⲩⲛ) fit the theological logic at moderate confidence. Genuinely unrestorable: the chapter title (0–2), the verb of speaking at line 2 (3), several long end-of-line lacunae (10, 11, 16, 26, 33, 35), the rubbed-off span at line 17, and unconstrained mid-line slots (6, 14, 19) where neither trace nor formula gives traction. The doctrinal payload is intact: every disorder the soul produces has its containment already established by the Lord, in advance.
